verdict.rationale: Stripe documents an official, first-party MCP server, which gives AI agents a sanctioned way to operate Stripe through natural-language requests from an MCP client. That counts as the product's own capability, but the evidence is only a single probe line: it does not show which Connect operations are exposed or how commands are interpreted, and there is no in-product natural-language interface. The llms.txt file only helps LLMs read the docs, so it is not credited as a way to operate the product. Missing for 10: documented natural-language command interface or assistant within Stripe Connect itself, details of Connect operations exposed via the MCP server, hands-on or independent corroboration of natural-language operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: official MCP server documented at https://docs.stripe.com/mcp
